properties.statement: Every congruence-identity-based failed approach draws its eliminating power from fixed-modulus congruence relations whose reach is structurally confined to quadratic non-residues, so the quadratic-residue classes survive every configuration of the method.

supporting_passages.quote: the QR wall is preserved by every congruence method
Blocked by the quadratic-reciprocity obstruction, not by search effort.
every failed family here preserves the quadratic-residue wall.

properties.preserved_distinctions: It does not merge the approaches' loci or operators: es-01 is class-local and constructive per residue class, es-12 is a global covering built on transversal solution forms, es-10 aggregates classes into a density statement, and es-08 is a meta-level obstruction analysis rather than a construction. They share only the confinement of congruence elimination to non-residues.
properties.contrast_check: The partial successes also touch this wall but differently: es-02 shares the congruence machinery and correspondingly reaches only almost-all primes, while es-07 dispatches 'Mordell-exceptional' quadratic-residue primes within its finite range, showing the confinement is a property of congruence-elimination methods rather than of the primes themselves. So the property discriminates by mechanism, not merely by topic.
properties.falsification: Exhibiting a fixed-modulus congruence identity family, or a finite covering assembled from such identities, that provably eliminates a quadratic-residue class would refute the claimed confinement.

properties.statement: These approaches operate in an aggregate or characterizing (existential) mode that explicitly gives up per-n construction, so they cannot certify a solution for any individual survivor prime even when their global statements are strong.

supporting_passages.quote: Distributional statement about many primes at once.
Local identities aggregated into a global thinness statement.
Constraint geometry of solutions; upstream of Type A/B systems.
Abstraction/transfer move; compression without added positivity.

properties.preserved_distinctions: The property does not merge their operators or uncertainty modes: es-05 is probabilistic ensemble averaging over primes, es-10 is deterministic density aggregation of identity-bearing classes, es-11 is algebraic constraint analysis of the solution set, and es-09 is an algebraic re-representation lift. They remain structurally distinct methods that share only the abandonment of per-n certification.
properties.contrast_check: Partial successes es-04 and es-06 are also existential in mode, so existential posture alone does not discriminate. The sharper contrast is es-07 (partial success), which is constructive and deterministic per n and produces certified per-instance solutions — exactly the capability the partial failures lack while still aiming at all n.
properties.falsification: An approach sharing this aggregate or characterizing posture that nonetheless yields a per-prime existence proof — for example an averaging bound with growth strong enough to force f(p) > 0 for every prime — would refute the claim that this posture participates in the stall.

properties.statement: The approach's payload is reorganization or compression of already-known mechanisms at a higher structural level, and by its own account this reorganization adds no new existence ('positivity') at the quadratic-residue wall.

supporting_passages.quote: prove that every prime admits at least one solution.
Strong evidence, not an existence proof.

properties.preserved_distinctions: es-09 unifies parameterizations as rational slices of one higher-dimensional variety (a representation change), while es-11 derives relations and symmetries within the solution set of the original representation (a constraint analysis); the property does not collapse re-representation into constraint mining.
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success note es-06 carries a near-identical annotation ('unifies methods but adds no positivity for QR primes'), so reorganization-without-positivity also occurs on the partial-success side. The difference is that es-06 additionally delivers representation lower bounds for almost all primes, whereas for es-09 and es-11 the reorganization is essentially the entire payload. This weakens the property from failure-cause to failure-symptom, which is why it ranks below the first two.
properties.falsification: A structural unification or lift in this family that produces an existence proof for a class previously uncovered — i.e., compression that demonstrably adds positivity — would refute the property.

properties.statement: The method's quantitative guarantee improves coverage monotonically (thinner exceptional sets, bounded averages) but its rate is structurally too weak to reach all n, leaving an infinite uncovered residue rather than a finite remainder.

supporting_passages.quote: Sharpens almost-all; does not reach all.

properties.preserved_distinctions: es-05 bounds an average of solution counts over a prime ensemble via sieve inequalities, while es-10 bounds the density of unsolved n by assembling identity-bearing classes; the shared asymptotic ceiling does not merge averaging with class assembly.
properties.contrast_check: Partial successes es-02 and es-06 also top out at almost-all coverage, so the ceiling itself is shared across outcome classes; what differs is that the partial-failure notes attribute the ceiling to an intrinsic rate limit of the method ('intrinsic to the method', 'never reaches zero'), not to unfinished work. The property therefore discriminates weakly and is ranked last.
properties.falsification: Showing that either bound can be strengthened past its stated rate limit — e.g., an average with polynomial growth or an exceptional-set bound reaching zero — would refute the claim that the ceiling is structural.
